chunks: ʿAlī ibn Muḥammad, from Muḥammad ibn ʿAlī ibn Ibrāhīm, from Abū ʿAbd Allāh ibn Ṣāliḥ.
That he saw him عليه السلام at the Black Stone, while the people were crowding and pulling toward it, and he عليه السلام was saying: “This is not what they were commanded to do.”

key_terms.الْحَجَرِ الْأَسْوَدِ: the Black Stone at the Kaʿbah
key_terms.يَتَجَاذَبُونَ: pulling and struggling against one another

ai.seo_question: What does the hadith mean by saying, “This is not what they were commanded to do” at the Black Stone?
ai.summary: This report describes a sighting of him عليه السلام near the Black Stone while people were pressing and struggling around it. His statement indicates disapproval of the manner in which people were behaving in that act of worship, pointing to the importance of observing the commanded form rather than emotional excess.

en.hubeali: Ali Bin Muhammad, from Muhammad Bin Ali Bin Ibrahim, from Abu Abdullah Bin Salih that,
‘He saw him<sup>asws</sup> by the Black Stone (Al-Hajr Al-Aswad), and the people were flocking upon it, and he<sup>asws</sup> was saying: ‘This is no what they have been Commanded with’.
en.sarwar: 7. Ali ibn Muhammad has narrated from Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Ibrahim from abu ‘Abdallah ibn Salih who has said the following.
“I saw him (the twelfth Imam) near the Black Stone while people were clinging over it. The Imam (a.s.) would say, “They are not commanded in this condition ( to kiss the Black Stone.”
